codeReview.summary: Reviewed the feature manifest, worker handoff, transcript skeleton for session `15fa3ec3-f381-412f-a26a-7374e7245d49`, and commit `11fc91e8887f35f5d8fb6fbbb8629bec3695a269`. The added regressions do cover the scoped project-admin behaviors at the route level, but the supposed durable-store coverage is implemented through a hand-rolled fake database rather than the real durable backend path. `createMockProjectDb()` stubs `execute()` to always return `{ rows: [] }` and only implements narrow in-memory `insert`/`select` behavior before `createDbBackedProjectStore()` injects that fake into `DbProjectStore`, so the new tests cannot catch durable-backend regressions in schema setup or actual query execution semantics.

issues.description: The new `createMockProjectDb()` harness turns the claimed durable-store coverage into an in-memory simulation. Because `execute()` is stubbed to always return `{ rows: [] }` and only a narrow `insert/select` subset is implemented before `DbProjectStore` is constructed, the tests never exercise the real durable Neon/Drizzle path, table setup, or query execution semantics that this feature was supposed to verify.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Durable-store follow-up work currently lacks a reusable real-backend verification pattern, which makes it easy for workers to substitute Drizzle AST or in-memory fakes while still claiming durable-path coverage.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: The committed test file introduces `createMockProjectDb()` and query-chunk parsing helpers (`services/auth-broker/tests/project-admin.test.ts:89-192`) instead of wiring `DbProjectStore` to an actual durable backend. The worker handoff also describes the change as a `deterministic mock database harness` rather than a live durable-store proof.

summary: Fail. The feature adds route-level regressions, but its new `DbProjectStore` tests rely on a fake in-memory database harness, so the claimed durable-backend parity is not actually verified.
